paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: nothing built on pride and greed gets to stay. Babylon said in her heart, "I sit as queen; I am not a widow and will never see grief." (Revelation 18:7) Then her plagues come "in one day," and "in a single hour" it's all gone (Revelation 18:8, 10). Everything that looked so permanent, the luxury, the splendor, the cargo, turned out to be sitting on nothing.

So the voice from heaven says, "Come out of her, My people, so that you will not share in her sins or contract any of her plagues." (Revelation 18:4) Notice that it's a call to God's own people, and it's urgent. I think that's a loving thing to say, because it's a warning given while there's still time to walk out. The question for you is simple: what are you leaning on, and who are you listening to?

And look at who gets the last word. The kings, the merchants and the sailors stand at a distance and mourn, but heaven is told, "Rejoice over her" (Revelation 18:20). Why? Because "God has pronounced for you His judgment against her." (Revelation 18:20) The blood of prophets and saints was found in her (Revelation 18:24), and God remembered it (Revelation 18:5). That's why I keep my ovens ready, friend: God sees what's done to His people, and He's faithful. This story isn't over yet.
